taskDescription: Arrange the steps of the visual cycle in rod cells in their correct order.
paragraphs: 11-cis-retinal binds to the protein opsin in a rod cell to form the visual pigment rhodopsin.
A photon of light converts 11-cis-retinal to all-trans-retinal, triggering a shape change that activates the G-protein transducin.
Activated transducin lowers cyclic GMP, closing sodium channels and hyperpolarising the rod cell to generate a nerve signal.
All-trans-retinal is released from opsin and reduced to all-trans-retinol.
All-trans-retinol is transported to the retinal pigment epithelium, where a multistep pathway regenerates 11-cis-retinal, which returns to the rod to bind opsin, completing the cycle.

overallFeedback.feedback: The visual cycle regenerates 11-cis-retinal from all-trans-retinal in a multi-step loop; when vitamin A is scarce, regeneration lags and rod sensitivity falls in dim light — this is why night blindness (nyctalopia) is the earliest clinical sign of deficiency.
